entities.summary: Eochaid mac Domnaill, also known as Eochaid Find, was a High King of Ireland who ruled Ailech from 565 to 571. He was the son of Domnall Ilchelgach, a member of the Cenél nEógain branch of the Uí Néill, and grandson of Muirchertach mac Muiredaig, a High King of Ireland. Eochaid's reign was marked by a series of military campaigns against the Picts and Scots, with whom he fought over control of the northern provinces. Despite his efforts, Eochaid was unable to secure a lasting victory, and his kingdom was eventually divided among his successors. Eochaid's legacy is still felt in the modern-day Irish language and culture, with many place names and surnames in Ireland still bearing the name of the Cenél nEógain. He was also mentioned in the Annals of Ulster, which provides valuable insights into his life and reign. Eochaid mac Domnaill's story serves as a reminder of the complexities and challenges faced by the ancient Irish kingdoms, and the enduring impact of their history on the modern world.
